entries.defect: VERDICT yes-under-conditions, not yet allowed: the bound stays 1 until the deciding test passes. Both halves agree the 1452 rule measured single-suite duration instead of acceptance throughput; a pair saves ~27 % wall clock on the M3 pairing (up to ~45 % balanced) at 1.5–3.5 % per-suite slowdown, pays while the overlap-added red rate stays under ~10 %, and the real gain is smaller (15–30 % of suite wall clock) because only both-backend passes and two points in acceptance pair; landed-point throughput stays unmeasured until the follow-up window.

EVIDENCE BASIS, resolved by the merger's code reading: B saw truncated material, A left the guard-credit question open. Checked: the both-backend guard scopes evidence to commits (coverageForHead keys on run.head ancestry, state at the common repo path, worktree receipts land in the main checkout), so a run from a same-SHA second worktree is credited — no blockade, no backlog item; ports and frame directories resolve per checkout (see U11, U12).

RISK shared frame directory and observation errors (verified: M3 ran both members in /workspace/hoa — the log names the partner FROM THIS CHECKOUT — and framesWritten rose from 2 quiet to 13/14 for water-stand-table and 28 to 30 for villager-dress). framesWrittenSince counts by mtime with no run identity, so a short run is masked and a wedged run's HUNG verdict is delayed; same-section pairs would overwrite frames; a newest-run wait can pick the peer and a cached receipt can make a trial run nothing. Certain in one checkout; absent across checkouts.

RISK and CONDITION load label: the second-started member is labelled loaded ('its timing verdicts do NOT count as evidence'), the first is not. Merged rule: a red stays a red — the label is informational for a pair member, never a reason to discount or retry; keep the default --on-load=flag (never defer, which skips the member; off is rejected because it drops the recorded label that proves the run was a pair member); the probe's wording is not rewritten under the freeze, the runbook states the reading.

RISK memory: idle ~16–17 % of 15.9 GB, villager-dress +49 points peaking in its last minute, water-stand-table +23; M3's 73–75 % holds only because the peaks did not coincide (coincident sum 89 %); two heavy sections ≈ 115 % = swap/OOM; full suites and LARGE unprofiled; 5 s sampling can miss spikes, hence the 80 % margin on measured peaks (U14).

RISK GPU contention is invisible on this host (one device via /dev/dxg for WebGPU and Mesa d3d12 WebGL 2; machine-load reports GPU load NOT measured). It shows only as slower frames → U7 reds and longer durations. B's request for GPU diagnostics is rejected as a test item (no counter exists); the load average and stray list the probe already prints are recorded per run, not judged.

RISK timing-sensitive checks: lower frame rate slips settle and shutter windows; the rotating adult-errands WebGL 2 checks (jar mouth, foam drift after shutter, walks on between frames, order-at-stand, sprint, heading-in-one-frame) are the probe. Comparison is per check name against a quiet baseline of the same build; steady charged signatures (render-verify-charges: 1456 rim/handover, water-stand-table WebGL 2 frames timeout) are excluded; an unstable quiet baseline leaves the combination unqualified instead of excusing loaded reds.

RISK backend extrapolation: WebGL 2 is noisier and more load-sensitive (villager-dress 6/9 vs 25/26) and M3 was WebGPU-only; no WebGPU result licenses WebGL 2, touch or voice pairing. The test therefore has WebGL 2 in three of four blocks and touch/voice stay excluded (U15).

LARGE stays exclusive — closing and bundle evidence, 115–121 min, unprofiled. Already enforced by run-logged's wait for a live LARGE wrapper in any worktree; VERIFY_NO_WAIT stays unused and short-section results never license a LARGE overlap.

RISK pictures: contention can catch late glTF arrival, LOD or unsettled camera without an assertion red. Merged test item: a person inspects every retained pair frame against its declared subject and compares usability with the quiet capture (not pixel equality); a missing, substituted or unusable required picture fails qualification; picture-stability is never calibrated from pair runs; M3's 28-vs-30 is explained by U3.

PORTS verified in _server.mjs: OS-assigned port (listen 0), vite --strictPort, one retry on a fresh port, BASE built from that port per run, Playwright on a pipe with a temporary profile; kill-tree per owning child. Nothing to re-tune; never pin --port. B's 'unverified' is closed.

CONDITION separate checkouts: each pair member runs in its own checkout (a worktree at the same SHA for one point's two backends) so verification/ (OUT resolves from _polish.mjs's own location), dist/ and the frame counter are separate. HOA_FRAME_DIR is no substitute because suites write to OUT. Guard credit across worktrees is confirmed (U2).

CONDITION same deps and immutable SHA: both checkouts identical in package.json, package-lock.json and vite.config.* (worktree-bootstrap's LINK condition already checks the lockfile; node_modules/.vite/deps is shared through the symlink); a dependency-changing branch runs solo; each acceptance run serves its final pushed SHA with nothing edited underneath. The render-verify-state last-writer race fails closed (a lost record costs a rerun) and is accepted.

CONDITION admission by pairing, not globally: a section/backend combination is admitted only when both have a measured solo memory profile and either idle + Δa + Δb ≤ 85 % or the measured pair peak stayed ≤ 80 % over ≥ 5 pairs; heavy+heavy (two villager-dress-class members) forbidden; section receipts keep their PARTIAL status and no whole-suite pairing follows from section results.
CONDITION never in a pair: LARGE and closing runs; benchmark, voice, touch, startup; picture-stability calibration runs; full polish suites until their solo memory profile is measured.

CONDITION nothing else heavy beside a pair: one owner schedules both members from the acceptance backlog; no build, lint or unit gate (M2 +12 %), no local author or agent, no third browser, no picture judgement during the pair; landing stays serial; a remote review (M1) is allowed beside ONE suite only — M1 was not measured beside a pair, so it is not allowed beside one until it is.

CONDITION memory sampled: the existing 1452 loop (MemTotal − MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo every 5 s, one shared log per pair, startup to cleanup) runs for every pair; a sample > 85 % aborts the later-started member; threshold no sample > 85 %, and ≤ 80 % for a pairing admitted on measured peaks; per-run start/end, makespan, backend, failures, frames and warnings come from the existing run.json and log.

STOP RULE: any uncharged red in an overlapped run, a sample > 85 %, a HUNG run, a crash, lost coverage or doubtful frame provenance switches pair mode off (bound 1); both members' evidence is kept; a red is never erased by a later green and no threshold or budget is relaxed as a remedy. Resumption: a quiet rerun of the red section on the same build attributes it — reproduces quiet → charged to its owning point, pairs resume; absent in 2 quiet runs → overlap-attributed, pairs stay off until diagnosed and filed. B's 'lost throughput advantage' is not a per-run trigger (noise); it is judged over the operational window (U24).

CONDITION waits name their log: run-wait.mjs <log> always (the newest-live default refuses when two runs are live, but naming the log is the rule); run-wait's expected-runtime values are re-measured only from the test's per-member durations (U24 keeps them valid) and failure budgets are never enlarged to make pairing pass.

TEST quiet references on the test build: solo memory profile (Δpeak above idle) per participating section/backend — villager-dress WebGPU and WebGL 2, water-stand-table WebGPU, water-jar-carried WebGL 2, adult-errands WebGL 2; duration and red references ≥ 3 each (villager-dress WebGPU 5, reusing existing same-build runs where the 1452 same-build diff holds), adult-errands WebGL 2 10 for the per-name base rate; every trial run with --again so no cached receipt answers instead; references run block-wise immediately before their pair block (B's interleaving) rather than all first (A), so host drift between reference and pair is bounded.

TEST protocol: one build (1452 same-build diff set), quiet host, no other heavy job, every run through run-logged.mjs, two separate checkouts, memory sampled; the later member starts 60 s after the first (A) and which section starts first alternates across repetitions (B); actual overlap intervals are read from the run.json startedAt/finishedAt. B's full-suite pairs are rejected for this test: full suites are excluded until profiled (U15) and whole-suite permission is a later measurement, not this one.

TEST pair blocks and statistics (resolves 12 pairs/B vs 13 pairs/A): 20 pairs in four blocks — 1 timing probe adult-errands WebGL 2 ×2 ‖ villager-dress WebGPU (5 partners, 10 probe runs); 2 mixed backend villager-dress WebGPU ‖ water-jar-carried WebGL 2 (7 pairs, the production both-backend case); 3 WebGL 2 + WebGL 2 water-jar-carried ‖ adult-errands (5 pairs, if U14 admits); 4 WebGPU + WebGPU villager-dress ‖ water-stand-table (3 pairs, M3 redone across checkouts). That gives 30 known-green member runs (villager-dress WebGPU 25/26, water-jar-carried 5/5, water-stand-table WebGPU 9/9): 0 overlap-attributed reds bounds the added red rate below 9.5 % at 95 %; 1 attributed red only passes after 15 further clean pairs (≥ 60 runs, ≈ 5 %); 2 attributed reds FAIL. Because the base rate is ~4 %, a plain red appears by chance in ~70 % of 30-run sets, so every red is attributed by the U18 quiet rerun before it counts. B's WebGL 2 villager-dress ‖ water-stand-table pair is rejected: water-stand-table WebGL 2 is red on every recent run (charged signature) and the coincident sum is 89 %, so it is neither a detector nor admissible. 20 pairs are a scoped pilot, not proof of zero added probability; qualified pairs stay under U18 in live use.

TEST timing probe (block 1): 10 overlapped adult-errands WebGL 2 runs against 10 quiet; per rotating check name count firings; FAIL if overlapped total > quiet + max(3, 50 % of quiet), or a name fires ≥ 2× overlapped that never fired quiet, or a one-sided Fisher test on any-rotating-red per run gives p < 0.10. Stated power: n = 10 per arm at a 20–40 % base detects about a 2× rise; if quiet shows a rotating red in more than 5 of 10 runs the section is no usable probe and WebGL 2 timing-sensitive pairing stays unqualified (WebGPU blocks may still qualify).

TEST thresholds (all must hold): no sample > 85 % (U17); 0 overlap-attributed reds per U22; probe per U23; every member's framesWritten equals its solo count on the same build (any cross-count FAIL); pair wall clock ≤ 0.80 × the sum of the two quiet medians (A's 0.80, stricter than B's 'sooner than the sum', because at 0.9 one false red eats the gain); each member ≤ 1.15 × its quiet median so run-wait's runtime expectations stay valid; each receipt names its own log, section, backend and load lines (U28). Order: block 1, 2, 3, 4, stop at first FAIL; ≈ 6.5–7 h host time (≈ 2.5–3 h references + ≈ 4 h pairs), ≈ 2 h if block 1 fails. Operational follow-up (B's T9 and A's T5 second half): after admission, wall clock per landed point over the runbook window (5 landed points or 48 h, whichever is later) against the post-1444 control of 2.53 h per point, counting diagnosis, repeats, picture work and waits once; pair mode stays only if not worse.

CHECK during the test, no new fields: each member's digest/receipt keeps its own failures, PARTIAL notice, backend and load lines and names its own log path (the digest has no loaded branch, so per-run separation already follows from the per-log record); a receipt that cannot be told from its peer's fails qualification.
